text:
sara_ops: heads up — customer on a private VPC (acct 9876) reports intermittent aborted streams and 502s when hitting our inference endpoint from their subnet. Only from their VPC, other networks are fine.

mike_dev: can you paste the client-side curl/tcp logs and the exact target URL? also which model/port are they hitting?

sara_ops: model=redwood/text-serve-1, host=api.private.redwood.example:443. curl -v from their bastion: 
```
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.private.redwood.example/v1/generate
*   Trying 10.8.5.34...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.private.redwood.example (10.8.5.34) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake starts
* TLS handshake complete, cipher=TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.private.redwood.example
> ...
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
* Connection #0 to host api.private.redwood.example left intact
* recv() returned 0, connection closed prematurely
* Closing connection 0
```
They also see stream chunks then connection closed with no error body.

lee_neteng: sounds like mid-stream RST/FIN from firewall or intermediate NAT. ask them to run this quick check: 
```
# from their bastion
sudo apt-get install -y traceroute tcpdump
traceroute -n 10.8.5.34
sudo timeout 15 tcpdump -i eth0 -w - 'tcp and host 10.8.5.34' | hexdump -C | head -n 200
```

sara_ops: they returned a small pcap snippet and traceroute. traceroute is a single hop (VPC internal). tcpdump shows initial 3-way handshake, TLS, then a TCP RST from source port 443 -> client highport (~53412) after ~1.2s. snippet: 
```
10:12:34.123456 IP 10.8.5.34.443 > 10.8.2.11.53412: RST, seq 0, win 0, length 0
10:12:34.124000 IP 10.8.2.11.53412 > 10.8.5.34.443: FIN, ack 1
```

mike_dev: that indicates server side (10.8.5.34) sent RST to client ephemeral port. Could be either our instance closing (OOM/serve bug) or a network firewall rewriting ports and breaking conntrack. Check instance syslogs and nginx/nginx-stream logs for process exits around that time.

infra-bot: noticed a NACL change on the customer's subnet 172.20.44.0/24 at 2024-03-07T10:10:20Z: rule 110 DENY outbound TCP ports 49152-65535 (temporary hardening). (auto-detect)

lee_neteng: that DENY on ephemeral outbound ports would block return path if NAT translation gives ephemeral source ports >49152. Stateful SG might allow, but NACL is stateless and will drop return packets. this is classic ephemeral returnpath mismatch.

sara_ops: ohh — customer says they rolled a hardened NACL for PCI scan. they can revert temporarily to confirm. in the meantime, any mitigation on our side?

mike_dev: we can attempt to keep connections on lower ephemeral range by binding to lower source ports? Not feasible. Better: ask customer to allow ephemeral high ports outbound, or add stateful NAT/allow rule. Recommend: allow 1024-65535 outbound or at least 49152-65535.

support_bot: suggested repro steps checklist: 1) confirm NACL outbound allow for ephemeral ports; 2) confirm no middlebox performing ephemeral port rewrite; 3) reproduce with tcpdump; 4) if blocked, whitelist our destination IP and ports in NACL and SG; 5) rollback PCI rule after scan.

sara_ops: customer temporarily removed the DENY for 49152-65535 and retried — streams are steady, no RSTs in tcpdump. Confirmed fix. They will patch their automation to permit ephemeral range then re-run scan with different rules.

lee_neteng: write up root cause: customer NACL stateless deny of high ephemeral outbound ports caused asymmetric return path (NAT assigned ephemeral >49152), leading to NACL dropping return packets and causing server to see/emit RSTs. Recommend documenting in private support KB.

mike_dev: adding quick note to internal KB and sending remediation checklist to customer support. :white_check_mark:

sara_ops: thanks all — closing this thread after KB entry. :thumbsup:
